candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this table states effluent discharge limits versus post-mixing instream concentration targets changes which numeric values are treated as enforceable discharge limits for exceedance comparison.

This header labels the acute aquatic column as a formula tied to effluent concentration Ce; interpreting it as the operative limit formula versus a descriptive calculation changes the derived numeric limit used for compliance comparison.
Whether Ce values in this column are enforceable effluent limits versus modeled or background concentrations determines which reported measurements are compared against a numeric discharge limit.

This row supplies Ce=10 plus multiple downstream criteria values (domestic 1, chronic aquatic 19/15, human health 30); different readings of which column is the applicable enforceable limit change the numeric threshold for exceedance determination.
Ce=2.11 coexists with much larger domestic and human-health criteria values; whether Ce or a criteria-column value governs changes the applicable numeric discharge limit for this parameter.
Ce=2.14 and domestic criteria 6 are both present; interpreting which is the operative enforceable limit changes the numeric threshold used in compliance comparison.

Method quantitation limits define the detection floor for listed parameters; their interpretation affects which monitoring methods/results are required (B) and whether absent or below-quantitation results are treated as documented no-data versus missing evidence (C).

This row lacks an MQL value and an effluent Ce value while listing chronic aquatic criteria 28 and 6.6; interpretation affects whether monitoring is required, which limit applies, and how missing or non-numeric results should be classified.

Whether the Need TMDL column indicates TMDL-driven limit or monitoring obligations changes which numeric limits are applicable and whether additional TMDL-related monitoring requirements are in scope.

Every listed pollutant shows N/A in the Need TMDL column; reading N/A as no TMDL-based obligation versus an unresolved TMDL status changes whether TMDL-linked limits or monitoring are treated as applicable.
This category label groups a subset of pollutants; whether it marks a distinct monitoring suite or analyte class changes which parameters are considered within required monitoring obligations.

The row has no Ce value but shows zeros in calculated instream columns and nonzero criteria values (domestic 70, human health 5300); interpreting zeros as no applicable limit versus not calculated, and choosing among criteria columns, changes limit applicability and missing-evidence classification.

These subheaders identify multiple parallel criteria families (domestic supply, chronic aquatic, human health); which family is operative for a given use/receiving water changes the enforceable numeric limit selected for comparison.

Placeholder-scale values appear in several criteria cells; reading them as no numeric limit, non-operative placeholders, or literal criteria changes whether a numeric compliance comparison is applicable and how absent results are categorized.
